# Running AIDE's solution tree on real data: can a research agent recover from failure?

Machine-learning engineering requires more than proposing a good experiment. A system must preserve failures, choose a useful next step, and evaluate alternatives. [AIDE](https://github.com/WecoAI/aideml) organizes solutions in a tree with Draft, Debug, and Improve operations. We reused components of its [published implementation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13138) on actual bike-rental counts, restricting the agent to a fixed estimator catalogue instead of executing arbitrary generated code.

![Experiment overview](/assets/research/ac052-cover.svg)

## Reusing the official search logic

We pinned the MIT-licensed repository at b39bb0e145e7785bcbc29e1b5d123f01d8f04c2c, verified source hashes, and extracted the exact Node, Journal, MetricValue and search_policy definitions using Python AST. The journal stores relationships, failures and metrics. The policy drafts when there are too few roots, may debug an eligible failed leaf, and otherwise improves the best valid node. We configured two drafts, debug probability one and maximum debug depth one to observe recovery, not to reproduce default performance.

We installed dataclasses-json and three dependencies, then checked compatibility of all 52 packages. An initial adapter error caused by missing AST location metadata was repaired. The upstream interpreter, full agent package and arbitrary generated Python were not executed.

## Data and a bounded experiment

The [UCI Bike Sharing dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/275/bike+sharing+dataset) (Fanaee-T, 2013, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.24432/C5W894) contains 731 daily rental aggregates. We trained on 365 days of 2011, validated on the first 183 days of 2012 and tested on the final 183. Ten calendar and weather features exclude casual and registered counts, which sum to the target. Observed same-day weather makes this retrospective prediction, not a prospective forecast under unknown weather.

The fixed catalogue contains nine Ridge, Random Forest and histogram-gradient-boosting settings. Both arms have eight attempts including a deliberately invalid first candidate and a shared Ridge baseline, leaving seven successful fits each. In the AIDE arm a local Qwen2.5:1.5b proposes an option from the remaining catalogue. Invalid options trigger a deterministic first-unseen fallback. The random arm chooses uniformly from unseen options. Attempt counts match, but compute, runtime and token budgets do not. We froze selection on validation RMSE before scoring test predictions, without a security-isolated evaluator.

![Observed solution tree](/assets/research/ac052-tree.svg)

## Results

| Policy | Validation RMSE | Test RMSE |
|---|---:|---:|
| Training mean | not computed | 3164.829 |
| AIDE + local LLM + fallback | 2134.192 | 2327.269 |
| Random | 2139.899 | 2325.086 |

![Test RMSE comparison](/assets/research/ac052-results.svg)

The native policy selected the deliberately failed leaf for debugging, then evaluated a valid forest configuration. Only two of six local-model proposals were valid; four required fallback. Recovery cannot be attributed to the LLM alone. The AIDE arm selected a marginally better validation model, but random search had a marginally better test RMSE by 2.18 rentals. With one paired seed and different proposal policies, no general search advantage is established.

Each execution completed 16 attempts and 14 fits. Replay reproduced every recorded value except elapsed time. A separate standard-library calculation verified test RMSE, and seven validation tests passed in normal and optimized Python.

## Implications for Anicca

Track proposal validity alongside performance and retain failed experiments. Next experiments should match proposal generators across search policies, validate structured outputs, measure actual compute and token budgets, and evaluate native code generation inside an isolated environment with an independent scorer. No Manager weights or product code changed. Remaining work is tracked in [issue #838](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-ops/issues/838).
